sections.name: NEW FEATURES
items: Verified per-game voice commands — 26 more games now have their own command set, checked against each game's real default PC keybinds and added alongside the generic Combat / Game / Menu / Navigation / Squad set. Starfield, World of Warcraft, WARDOGS (including its Ground Vehicle and Rotary Vehicle schemes), Call of Duty: Warzone, Valorant, Apex Legends, CS2, Halo Infinite, Battlefield 2042, Escape from Tarkov, Squad, Elden Ring, Path of Exile 2, Destiny 2, Fortnite, Final Fantasy XIV, Gray Zone Warfare, Icarus, Minecraft, Overwatch 2, Rocket League, Rust, Schedule 1, theHunter: Call of the Wild, Valheim and Windrose. Where a game's key differs from a generic command of the same name, the game gets a distinct phrase instead (for example CS2 uses "pushtotalk" and "sneak", Rocket League has "boost")

sections.name: IMPROVEMENTS
items: More keys can be sent — the keyboard output now knows L, P, NumLock, O, PageUp, PageDown, K, Left Ctrl, U, N, T, Caps Lock, D, Up Arrow and Down Arrow, which the new game commands need
Voice mute now silences everything — hotkey-triggered voice lines and ambient barks are muted along with commands, so "mute" really means quiet until you say "unmute"
The ambience-bed (haunt) layer also looks for a haunt_<word> clip in your PC Commands pack, so a PC pack can supply its own
The headless engine (launched from CaliberHQ) shows no window at all again. The status HUD that 0.8.9 described was removed, so the engine now runs silently in the background

sections.name: BUG FIXES
items: MIN and CLOSE on the engine window each fire once — the injected script now replaces the inline click handler instead of adding a second one on top of it

sections.name: NEW FEATURES
items: Voice mute — say "mute" and the engine stops acting on anything you say (no keys, no text, no commands, no PC commands) until you say "unmute". The mic stays on the whole time so it can hear you come back; this is separate from CaliberHQ's hard mic stop. "mute" needs the exact word so it can't trip mid-game; "unmute" is loose — "unmute, ok where was I" resumes and you carry straight on. Each toggle speaks an acknowledgement in your PC Commands voice (drop pc_mute / pc_unmute clips into a PC pack to use a recording instead of the built-in Windows voice). Exposed on GET /status as "muted"

Narration voice packs — reactive character lines the engine can't detect on its own now have a home. Say a callout phrase ("tally", "wasted", "reloading", "low ammo", "spotted", "man down", "sitrep") to play a random line from that bucket; Space / Starfield / No Man's Sky flavour and idle musings fold into the ambient-bark timer, which now counts a pack's real ambient line count instead of assuming ten. First pack built this way: Divergence-7

sections.name: IMPROVEMENTS
items: The status HUD now shows when the engine is launched from CaliberHQ (headless) — before, it only existed in the standalone app. It reports listening state, the last command, and the active profile; clicking it brings CaliberHQ back to the front. The minimize button is hidden in this mode
HUD POSITION takes effect immediately — picking a corner in CaliberHQ's Settings moves the HUD right away instead of only on its next appearance

build_voicepack.py strips a pack's own name prefix when parsing filenames, so a Caliber Voice Studio export like "divergence_7_general_enemy_spotted_03" reads the trigger as "general_enemy_spotted" rather than swallowing the "7_"

sections.name: BUG FIXES
items: The mic can no longer keep hearing commands after a stop — StartListening now disposes any stale capture object instead of leaving a second one attached, and StopListening always clears the field even if teardown throws

sections.name: NEW FEATURES
items: PC Commands — say (or type) a trigger phrase to launch something on your PC and get a spoken acknowledgement back in your character's voice. Each entry maps a phrase to an action (open a URL, launch an app or shell URI, or send a key combo like Win+E / Ctrl+Shift+Esc) plus an optional spoken line. Edit the list in CaliberHQ under Voice Packs → PC Commands, as a global list and/or per-profile (a profile entry wins over a global one with the same trigger)

PC-command voice packs — a second pack per character (e.g. "'Shade' PC Commands") holds the acknowledgement lines, kept separate from the game pack and chosen in CaliberHQ (PC Commands pane or Settings). Missing a line falls back to a custom typed line spoken by the built-in Windows voice, then to the trigger word
Send-a-command: run any phrase — a game command or a PC Command — straight through the engine from CaliberHQ with no mic, via the new POST /api/caliberengine/process-text endpoint

sections.name: IMPROVEMENTS
items: Voice packs now play .mp3 as well as .wav, so a raw Caliber Voice Studio "Export Pack" zip drops straight into voicepacks/<name>/ with no conversion step

KeyboardOutput can send Windows-shortcut keys — the Windows key, PrintScreen, the nav cluster, and media/volume keys — with the extended-key flag, so combos like Win+E and Ctrl+Shift+Esc register reliably

CaliberHQ Command Guide reworked — a three-part header (turbine lockup, the active voice pack, a dark/light toggle for printing), fixed table column widths so every section lines up, and a footer mark

sections.name: BUG FIXES
items: The mute / listening toggle in CaliberHQ now works while the engine runs headless — the headless API was never wired for start/stop (and was also missing the game list, PC Commands, and process-text). The GUI and headless instances are now wired identically

sections.name: NEW FEATURES
items: Haunt layer — an opt-in per-profile atmospheric echo. When it's on, saying any word the active pack has a haunt_<word> whisper for plays that whisper over whatever audio is already going — no key, no typed text, no command fired. Toggle it per profile in CaliberHQ's Voice Packs pane, or set "HauntLayerEnabled": true in the profile JSON. Off by default with zero overhead when off; the Apparition and Phantom packs ship with 11 whisper words built in
Two new characters — Phantom (formerly "The Wretch") and Apparition — each with ARPG, Mistfall Hunter, MMO, and General script sets
ARPG standard command layer — 33 genre-common triggers (skill 1-6, potion, town portal, waypoint, salvage, identify, force-move, mount, character, skill tree, vendor) any ARPG profile can use

Voice pack scripts added for Mistfall Hunter (58 triggers / 188 lines — ARPG combat, the mist/extract loop, enemy classes and Mist Lords) and Rust (108 triggers / 338 lines — building, crafting, electricity, vehicles, farming, plus monument and threat callouts)
